autoLaunchTab.climbExitDesc: Climb behavior and transition to normal flight
autoLaunchTab.detectTimeHint: Must exceed threshold for this duration. Default: 40ms
autoLaunchTab.detectionDesc: Thresholds to detect when aircraft is thrown/launched

autoLaunchTab.headerDesc: Configure automatic launch detection for throw, bungee, or catapult launches. When enabled via a switch, the FC detects the launch and automatically climbs to a safe altitude.
autoLaunchTab.idleDelayHint: Delay before idle motors spin. Default: 0ms

autoLaunchTab.maxAngleHint: Max pitch/roll to accept launch. 180 = disabled. Default: 45°

autoLaunchTab.safety1: Always test auto launch in an open area with plenty of clearance
autoLaunchTab.safety2: Start with conservative settings and adjust based on your aircraft
autoLaunchTab.safety3: Ensure NAV LAUNCH mode is assigned to a switch before using
autoLaunchTab.safety4: Have a way to abort (disarm switch or manual override)
autoLaunchTab.spinupHint: Ramp time from idle to launch throttle. Default: 100ms

autoLaunchTab.wiggleHint: Yaw wiggle to start idle motor

filterConfigTab.subtitle: Configure noise filtering for smooth and clean flight
filterConfigTab.tipDTerm: D-Term: More aggressive filtering here reduces motor heat and oscillations.
filterConfigTab.tipDynNotch: Dynamic Notch: Automatically tracks motor noise. Set min/max to bracket your motor frequencies.
filterConfigTab.tipLowpass: Lowpass: Lower values = more filtering, less noise, but more delay. Start at 150Hz.
filterConfigTab.title: Filter Configuration

motorMixerTab.emptyMultiHint: Pick a frame type above to get started. Most drones use "Quad X" - the standard layout with 4 motors in an X shape.
motorMixerTab.emptyPlaneHint: Pick a motor setup above. Most airplanes have a single motor - control surfaces handle steering.
motorMixerTab.legendHint: Numbers in the diagram match motor outputs on your flight controller (M0, M1, etc.). Opposite motors spin in opposite directions to cancel torque.

preset.hexBeginner: Six motors provide more power and redundancy. If one motor fails, you might still be able to land safely.
preset.quadPlaneVTOLBeginner: VTOL aircraft: 4 lifting motors (like a quad) plus 1 pusher motor for forward flight. Most popular VTOL setup.
preset.quadPlusBeginner: Motors are arranged in a + shape. One motor points forward. Less common but works well for some frames.
preset.quadXBeginner: This is what most racing and freestyle drones use. The X shape gives balanced control in all directions.
preset.singleMotorBeginner: Most airplanes have one motor at the front (tractor) or back (pusher). Control surfaces handle steering.
preset.triVTOLBeginner: VTOL with 3 motors that tilt for transition. Lighter than QuadPlane but more complex mechanically.
preset.twinMotorDiffBeginner: Two wing motors spinning opposite directions. Yaw is controlled by speeding up one motor and slowing the other.
preset.twinMotorRudderBeginner: Two wing motors at equal speed. Use this if your plane has a rudder/tail for yaw control.

motorMixerTab.questionMulti: What type of frame do you have?
motorMixerTab.questionPlane: How many motors does your airplane have?
motorMixerTab.rotationInfo: Rotation direction is inferred from mixing values: motors with positive roll mix spin CW (orange), negative roll spin CCW (blue). For airplanes, yaw mixing is used instead.
motorMixerTab.subtitle: Configure motor output mixing
motorMixerTab.title: Motor Mixer
motorMixerTab.whatIsMulti: Motor mixer tells your flight controller how each motor should respond when you move the sticks. Pick a preset that matches your frame shape.
motorMixerTab.whatIsPlane: Motor mixer controls how your motor(s) respond to throttle. Most airplanes have one motor - control surfaces handle steering.

header.title: {{firmware}} Tuning

m0.beginner: SAFETY SWITCH - Arms/disarms your aircraft. Always have this on a switch!

m1.beginner: BEGINNER MODE - Aircraft stays level automatically. Best for learning!

m10.beginner: Return To Home - Aircraft will climb to safe altitude and fly back to launch point. Essential safety feature!

m11.beginner: GPS position hold - Aircraft will stay in place. Great for aerial photography or when you need to stop.

m12.beginner: Direct servo/motor control without stabilization. For experienced pilots only!

m13.beginner: Makes your aircraft beep - great for finding it in grass!

m2.beginner: TRAINING MODE - Self-levels at center, allows flips at full stick

m21.beginner: Automatically tunes PID values during flight

m26.beginner: Records flight data for tuning analysis

m27.beginner: EMERGENCY MODE - Triggers failsafe behavior. Normally activated automatically when signal is lost.

m28.beginner: Execute uploaded waypoint mission. Aircraft will fly to each waypoint automatically.

m29.beginner: Keeps full stick authority even at zero throttle. Essential for freestyle tricks and flips.

m3.beginner: Holds current altitude using barometer/GPS. Throttle controls climb/descent rate.

m30.beginner: Sets current position as new home point. Use when you relocate during a session.

m31.beginner: Allow ground control station to send navigation commands (fly-to-here, etc).

m34.beginner: Activates flaperons for slower landing approach. Ailerons droop down to act as flaps.

m35.beginner: Auto-coordinates rudder with ailerons for smooth turns. Great for fixed-wing beginners.

m36.beginner: Automatic launch sequence for fixed-wing. Throw the plane and it will climb to safe altitude.

m37.beginner: Automatically adjusts servo trim during flight

m45.beginner: Fixed-wing cruise mode - Maintains heading and altitude. Perfect for long-range flights.

m46.beginner: Aggressive braking when releasing sticks on multirotor

m5.beginner: Maintains current magnetic heading. Useful for flying straight lines.

m51.beginner: Safety switch - must be enabled before arming. Prevents accidental arm.

m52.beginner: Flip crashed aircraft back over using motor spin. For multirotors only.

m53.beginner: Maintains current heading while allowing altitude control. Good for flying in a straight line.

m55.beginner: Enable in-flight waypoint planning via stick commands.

m56.beginner: Enables thermal detection and circling for gliders

m6.beginner: Stick directions are relative to pilot, not aircraft - useful for beginners

modes.howThisWorks: How this works: Each mode is triggered by a switch on your transmitter. Move your switches to see which modes activate. The bar shows where your switch needs to be.

pidTab.dHelp: Dampens overshooting. Too high = hot motors and noise. Too low = bouncy stops.
pidTab.iHelp: Keeps your quad on target. Helps fight wind and drift. Too high = slow wobbles.
pidTab.pHelp: How quickly your quad reacts. Too high = oscillation/vibration. Too low = mushy feeling.

portsTab.howItWorks: <h>How this works: </h>Each row is a physical UART connector on your board. Enable <c>RX</c> on the UART your receiver is wired to. Set <c>Sensors</c> for GPS or rangefinder, and <c>Peripherals</c> for OSD or VTX control. Save and reboot to apply.
portsTab.setupDji: DJI goggles: Set <c>Peripherals → MSP Displayport</c> on the DJI UART
portsTab.setupGps: GPS module: Set <c>Sensors → GPS</c> on the UART it's connected to, baud <c>115200</c>
portsTab.setupSbus: SBUS receiver: Enable <c>RX</c> on the UART with the SBUS pad (usually has a built-in inverter)
portsTab.softSerialWarning: Soft serial ports have limited bandwidth and are not suitable for high-speed protocols like CRSF or GPS.
portsTab.subtitle: Configure UART functions. Only one port can have Serial RX enabled. Save + reboot to apply.
portsTab.title: UART Port Configuration

receiverTab.channelMappingHint: This controls which stick axis maps to which channel. If moving your throttle stick shows the wrong bar in Live RC above, pick a different preset here. Most receivers use AETR. JR/Spektrum radios use TAER.
receiverTab.checkPowered: Receiver is powered and bound to transmitter
receiverTab.checkUart: Correct UART is configured for Serial RX
receiverTab.deadbandHint: A small zone around stick center where tiny movements are ignored. Increase if your drone drifts when sticks are centered. Default of 0 is fine for most setups.
receiverTab.noSerialRxBody: INAV turns the receiver off at the next boot when no port carries Serial RX, and the receiver type falls back to None. Enable RX on the UART your receiver is wired to.
receiverTab.noSerialRxTitle: No UART has Serial RX enabled
receiverTab.protocolHint: Your transmitter sends stick commands to a small receiver wired to your flight controller. Select the protocol that matches your receiver. Check the label on your receiver if unsure.

receiverWizard.descCrsf: CRSF protocol - most popular for long range FPV
receiverWizard.descIbus: FlySky serial protocol - simple and reliable
receiverWizard.descMsp: Receive RC via MSP from ground station or simulator
receiverWizard.descSbus: Inverted serial - requires UART with built-in inverter

safetyTab.inavNavNote: iNav's advanced navigation features (RTH, waypoints, position hold) are configured in the Navigation tab. The failsafe RTH option above uses those settings.
